title: A customer status field that exists twice
prompt:
A legacy SOAP service returns customer records. Each `<cust:Customer>` element carries a business `id` attribute, a `<cust:Name>`, and a `<cust:Status>` (its lifecycle status, e.g. `ACTIVE`). Some records also carry an unrelated `<audit:Status>` from a separate compliance system, sitting as a sibling of `<cust:Status>` — it is a different field that happens to share the same local name.

Return an array of `{ id, name, status }`, where `status` is always the **customer** status (the `cust` namespace one), never the audit one, regardless of which element comes first in the document.

The two namespaces are declared on the root `<soap:Envelope>` element; read the sample input to find their URIs.

<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:cust="http://acme.com/customer" xmlns:audit="http://acme.com/audit">
  <soap:Body>
    <cust:GetCustomersResponse>
      <cust:Customer id="C-1">
        <cust:Name>Alice Chen</cust:Name>
        <audit:Status>REVIEWED</audit:Status>
        <cust:Status>ACTIVE</cust:Status>

  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>

<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:cust="http://acme.com/customer" xmlns:audit="http://acme.com/audit">

hints: A bare selector like `.Status` matches on local name only — it does not care which namespace the element actually belongs to.
When two different elements in the same document share a local name but live in different namespaces, a bare selector cannot tell them apart. It has to pick one.

Declare `ns cust ...` and `ns audit ...` for both URIs found on the root element, then select with `cust#Status` instead of `Status` so the namespace is part of what you're matching, not just the name.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
ns audit http://acme.com/audit
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.cust#Status
}

mustFail.why: uses a bare .Status selector, which matches whichever Status element (cust or audit) happens to come first in document order
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.Status
}

explanation.approach: A namespace-qualified element is identified by its local name AND its namespace URI together — the two form one key. But a selector written without a namespace prefix, like `.Status`, only ever asks about the local name. When a document has exactly one element with that local name, the distinction never comes up and the bare selector looks perfectly fine. It only breaks once a second element with the same local name — in a different namespace — enters the document, and it breaks silently: it just returns whichever one appears first, with no error to flag the ambiguity.

snippets.label: Two elements, same local name, different namespaces
snippets.note: The bare `.Status` selector matches `a:Status` simply because it is the first sibling in the document — not because it belongs to any particular namespace. `b:Status` is silently skipped.

snippets.label: Qualifying both selectors resolves the ambiguity
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns a http://a.com
ns b http://b.com
---
{ aStatus: payload.root.a#Status, bStatus: payload.root.b#Status }
snippets.note: Once each selector names both the prefix and the local name, each one reaches exactly the element it means.

snippets.label: The wrong approach on the sample input
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.Status
}
snippets.payload:
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:cust="http://acme.com/customer" xmlns:audit="http://acme.com/audit">
  <soap:Body>
    <cust:GetCustomersResponse>
      <cust:Customer id="C-1">
        <cust:Name>Alice Chen</cust:Name>
        <audit:Status>REVIEWED</audit:Status>
        <cust:Status>ACTIVE</cust:Status>
      </cust:Customer>
      <cust:Customer id="C-2">
        <cust:Name>Bob Martinez</cust:Name>
        <audit:Status>FLAGGED</audit:Status>
        <cust:Status>SUSPENDED</cust:Status>
      </cust:Customer>
    </cust:GetCustomersResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
snippets.note: Both customers come back with the audit system's status instead of their own, because in this feed `audit:Status` happens to be written before `cust:Status` inside each `Customer`. The output is well-formed JSON with plausible-looking values — nothing about it looks like a bug.

snippets.label: The same bug is invisible when the audit field is absent
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.Status
}
snippets.note: With no `audit:Status` sibling, `cust:Status` is the only element with that local name, so the bare selector reaches it and the wrong script happens to produce the right answer. A test suite built only from records like this one would never catch the bug.

snippets.label: The correct, namespace-qualified extraction
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
ns audit http://acme.com/audit
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.cust#Status
}
snippets.payload:
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:cust="http://acme.com/customer" xmlns:audit="http://acme.com/audit">
  <soap:Body>
    <cust:GetCustomersResponse>
      <cust:Customer id="C-1">
        <cust:Name>Alice Chen</cust:Name>
        <audit:Status>REVIEWED</audit:Status>
        <cust:Status>ACTIVE</cust:Status>
      </cust:Customer>
      <cust:Customer id="C-2">
        <cust:Name>Bob Martinez</cust:Name>
        <audit:Status>FLAGGED</audit:Status>
        <cust:Status>SUSPENDED</cust:Status>
      </cust:Customer>
    </cust:GetCustomersResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
snippets.note: `cust#Status` names the namespace as part of the selector, so it reaches the customer's own status regardless of which sibling was written first.
